cases.question: Is there a discount for new customers at the moment?
cases.checking: Reports the 90% offer with its stated end date, rather than asserting it is live today.
cases.answer: Yes — as retrieved on 14 September 2026, Xero's pricing pages advertised new-customer discounts in the two regions covered by the evidence. On the Australian pricing page, new customers get 90% off for the first 3 months, after which Xero's regular price applies and the subscription auto-renews monthly until cancelled (E1). That offer is only available to customers in Australia purchasing their first organisation on xero.com, runs until 11:59pm AEST on 30 September 2026 using code DC9032619AU, and applies to base Ignite, Grow, Comprehensive, Ultimate or Ultra plan subscriptions; it does not apply to additional charges for add-ons, usage and payment fees unless otherwise specified (E1). On the United States pricing page, new customers get 90% off for the first 6 months, then the regular price applies and the subscription auto-renews monthly until cancelled (E2). The US offer is available until 30 September 2026 at 11:59pm UTC using code DC90626308US, only for customers in the United States purchasing their first organization on xero.com, and applies to base Early, Growing and Established plan subscriptions, again excluding additional charges for add-ons, usage and payment fees unless otherwise specified (E2). Both pages state that the offer cannot be used with or exchanged for any other offer and that Xero can change or cancel the offer at any time (E1, E2). The evidence does not show pricing or promotional terms for any region other than Australia and the United States.
cases.notes: The discounted-offer passages are region-specific: E1 is the Australian pricing page (passage metadata: region AU, currency AUD) and E2 is the United States pricing page (passage metadata: region US, currency USD); both were retrieved on 2026-09-14. The offer terms in E1 and E2 differ in length of discount (3 months vs 6 months), time zone of expiry (AEST vs UTC) and eligible plan names, so they should not be read as one global offer. E1's discount percentage figures and expiry are as written in that passage; no currency amounts appear in these passages. Passage E3, E4, E5 and E6 contain general company/background material and no promotional terms.

cases.answer: Xero's cost depends on the region and plan shown in each passage. For the US (USD, as retrieved 2026-09-14), the passage labelled "Established" lists $9 per month for the first 6 months, then $90 per month (E1), and the passage labelled "Early" lists $2.50 per month, then $25 per month, with an optional item listed at $36 a month + $6 per employee/contractor (E2). The US passages also state that Xero subscription prices are increasing from October 1, 2026 (E2). For Australia (AUD, as retrieved 2026-09-14), Grow is listed at $7.80 per month then $78 per month (E4), and for the first 3 months at $7.80 per month before rising to $78 per month (E5); Comprehensive is listed at $10.70 per month, then $107 per month (E6); and Ultimate 10 is listed at $14.30 per month, then $143 per month (E3). The US passage states all prices are listed in USD and do not include applicable taxes (E2), while the Australian pricing-plans passage states prices are in AUD and include GST (E4). Beyond these specific figures, the passages do not set out a single complete price list for Xero.
cases.notes: Region and currency: passages E1 and E2 are US pricing in USD; passages E3, E4, E5 and E6 are Australian pricing in AUD. All passages were retrieved on 2026-09-14; prices are described as current as of that retrieval and Xero reserves the right to change pricing at any time (E2, E4). cases.answer:
Pricing and plans are shown separately for each region, and the passages cover two regions only. On Xero's Australian pricing page (region AU, currency AUD, as retrieved 2026-09-14), the plan names shown are Grow, Comprehensive and Ultimate 10 (E1). The Grow plan is listed as "$7.80 per month" then "$78 per month", and its listed inclusions are Smart document capture basic extraction, Payroll for 2 people, a 60 day cashflow forecast, and claiming expenses and mileage for 1 user (E1). The page states that prices are in AUD and include GST, that Xero reserves the right to change pricing at any time, and that subscriptions auto-renew monthly until cancelled (E1). It also states that if you later decide to change to a less expensive plan you can do so 1 month after upgrading, and that additional charges may apply if you go over the stated included number of users (Expenses and Projects) or people paid (Payroll) (E1). The same AU page advertises that if you purchase any Xero plan, the first month is free (E4). Separately, the AU accounting software page says Xero offers several plans to suit different business sizes and needs and invites users to visit the pricing page to compare plans and start a 30-day free trial (E6).

On Xero's US pricing page (region US, currency USD, as retrieved 2026-09-14), the plan names shown are Early, Growing and Established (E3). The Early plan is listed as "$2.50 per month" then "$25 per month", with inclusions of sending quotes and 20 invoices†, 5 bills, reconciling bank transactions, visualising performance with basic graphs, and a 30 day cash flow forecast (E3). The US page states that subscription prices are increasing from October 1, 2026, that all prices are listed in USD and do not include applicable taxes, and that taxes will be calculated based on your billing address (E3). It also shows free ACH, with fees applying for other payment methods (E3), and lists payroll as optional at "$36 a month + $6 per employee/contractor" (E3). On the AU page, payroll appears as an included item on Grow ("Payroll for 2 people") (E1).

On features, the AU accounting software page describes Xero as cloud-based accounting software that can be logged into wherever there is an internet connection, and says Xero handles tracking income and expenses, managing invoices, reconciling bank transactions and preparing financial reports (E6). It states Xero is ATO-certified for STP, automatically calculates GST and generates pre-filled activity statements that can be lodged directly with the ATO (E6), and that Xero lets you connect your bank accounts, with most banks connectable automatically via a secure direct feed for daily updates, and manual import of bank statements where automatic bank feeds are not available (E6). The AU pricing page describes a tool that asks a little about your business and points you to the right plan in under two minutes (E2), and the AU accounting software page quotes customer reviews praising automated bank feeds, invoicing features and easy reconciliation (E5).
cases.notes: Pricing is region- and time-specific. The AU passages (E1, E2, E4, E5, E6) are region AU, currency AUD, retrieved 2026-09-14T08:30:17–19Z, and E1 states prices are in AUD and include GST. The US passage (E3) is region US, currency USD, retrieved 2026-09-14T08:30:18Z, and states prices are in USD and exclude applicable taxes. Figures are quoted exactly as they appear, including the † and †† markers. The user message repeated the same question many times; the passages contained no embedded instructions to act on.
